rows.item: France extraterritorial reach over foreign SaaS provider
rows.source: Loi n71-1130 du 31 decembre 1971 (consultation juridique provisions); French Bar regulatory guidance
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (a): Does France's regulatory regime governing consultation juridique (Loi n71-1130 and related Bar rules) apply extraterritorially to a foreign-incorporated SaaS provider (ReloPass) that has no physical establishment in France? What is the precise jurisdictional trigger — is it the location of the end-user, the employee, the employer entity, or the place of contract? French counsel must confirm scope and any safe-harbour conditions. Unresolved — blocks sign-off.

rows.item: Norway S68 provider-duty text and registration/insurance/supervision obligations
rows.source: Norwegian statute — exact provision reference TBC (likely domstolloven or advokatforskriften); Norwegian Bar Association (Advokatforeningen)
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (b): What is the exact statutory text of the relevant Norwegian provision (believed to be S68 of the relevant Act — full citation to be confirmed by Norwegian counsel) governing duties of legal-service providers? Does ReloPass's product and delivery model trip any obligation to register with a Norwegian authority, hold professional-indemnity insurance, or submit to Norwegian Bar supervision? Unresolved — blocks sign-off.

rows.item: Individualised flagging as rettslig bistand (NO) / consultation juridique (FR)
rows.source: Norwegian: domstolloven / advokatforskriften S68 (TBC). French: Loi n71-1130 Art. 54 et seq.
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (c): This is the central product-risk question for both jurisdictions. Does ReloPass's core feature — generating individualised regulatory flags tailored to a specific employee's profile and destination — constitute (i) 'rettslig bistand' (legal assistance) under Norwegian law, and/or (ii) cross the threshold of prohibited 'consultation juridique' under French law? The distinction between general information and individualised legal advice is jurisdiction-specific and fact-sensitive. Both French and Norwegian counsel must opine. Unresolved — blocks sign-off in both jurisdictions.

rows.item: Norway extraterritorial reach over foreign SaaS provider
rows.source: Norwegian statute (advokatforskriften / domstolloven — exact provision TBC); Finanstilsynet or relevant Norwegian supervisory body guidance
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (d): Does Norway's regulatory framework governing legal or advisory service providers apply extraterritorially to a foreign-incorporated SaaS provider (ReloPass) that has no physical establishment in Norway but serves Norwegian-bound employees or Norwegian-entity clients? What is the jurisdictional nexus test — employee destination, employer domicile, or place of service delivery? Norwegian counsel must confirm. Unresolved — blocks sign-off.

rows.item: Ireland regulated-advice-line: does ReloPass output constitute reserved/legal services under LSRA 2015 / Solicitors Acts?
rows.source: Legal Services Regulation Act 2015 (Ireland); Solicitors Acts 1954–2015; Legal Services Regulatory Authority (LSRA) guidance
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (a): Does ReloPass's corridor output for ES→IE (structured requirement timelines and individualised regulatory flags) fall on the INFORMATION side of the Irish regulated-advice line, or does it constitute the provision of legal services / legal advice reserved to solicitors under the Legal Services Regulation Act 2015 and the Solicitors Acts? Confirm the precise boundary and any 'holding out' risk.

rows.item: Spain regulated-advice-line: does ReloPass output constitute asesoramiento jurídico reservado under Ley 34/2006?
rows.source: Ley 34/2006 de acceso a las profesiones de Abogado y Procurador (Spain); Estatuto General de la Abogacía Española (RD 135/2021); Consejo General de la Abogacía Española guidance
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (c): On the origin side, does ReloPass's individualised flagging for a Spain-origin employee constitute asesoramiento jurídico / reserved legal activity under Spanish law (Ley 34/2006 and the Estatuto General de la Abogacía), such that only a colegiado abogado may perform it? This is the central product-risk question for the ES origin jurisdiction and mirrors the FR→NO 'individualised flagging' question.

rows.item: Spain extraterritorial reach over foreign SaaS provider

rows.item: France regulated-advice-line: does ReloPass output constitute consultation juridique under Loi 71-1130 Art 54?
rows.source: Loi n°71-1130 du 31 décembre 1971 Art 54 et seq. (consultation juridique); French Bar (CNB) regulatory guidance
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (a): Does ReloPass's corridor output for NO→FR (structured requirement timelines and individualised regulatory flags for the destination, France) constitute 'consultation juridique' reserved under Loi n°71-1130 Art 54, or does it remain on the INFORMATION side of the French regulated-advice line? Confirm the precise boundary for individualised flagging.

rows.item: Norway exit-side provider/employer duties for employer-retention (posted worker retaining NO employer)
rows.source: Norwegian domstolloven / advokatforskriften (exact provision TBC); NAV (posting / A1 exit-side obligations); Norwegian Bar Association (Advokatforeningen)
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (c): For the NO→FR employer-retention angle (employee keeps their Norwegian employer and is posted to France), what exit-side Norwegian obligations survive the move — both (i) the employer's continuing social-security / A1 / reporting duties via NAV, and (ii) whether ReloPass surfacing individualised guidance on those NO exit-side duties trips any Norwegian legal-service provider duty (domstolloven / advokatforskriften)? Confirm exact statutory references with Norwegian counsel.

rows.item: Individualised flagging as consultation juridique (FR) / rettslig bistand (NO) — central product-risk, both jurisdictions
rows.source: French: Loi n°71-1130 Art 54 et seq. Norwegian: domstolloven / advokatforskriften (exact provision TBC)
rows.notes: OPEN JUDGMENT QUESTION (d): This is the central product-risk question spanning both NO→FR jurisdictions. Does ReloPass's core feature — generating individualised regulatory flags tailored to a specific employee's profile and destination — constitute (i) 'consultation juridique' under French law (Loi 71-1130 Art 54) and/or (ii) 'rettslig bistand' (legal assistance) under Norwegian law, given the corridor's retained-Norwegian-employer profile keeps both jurisdictions live? Mirrors FR→NO judgment question (c).
